entries.locator: Problem equations (1)-(3) and Comment; record dated 15 September 2026.
entries.note: The catalogue asks for the minimal length of a symmetric qubit code encoding one qubit and correcting two arbitrary errors. A proof for a narrower code family leaves a gap. The listed status is a catalogue designation.

entries.locator: Proposition 7.1 and Section 7; Theorem 5.3 and Example 5.
entries.note: For an odd-length real, parity-separated family, Proposition 7.1 reduces correction conditions to quadratic equations. Section 7 reports a nineteen-qubit solution obtained with msolve intervals enclosing a genuine root, with a Mathematica cross-check. Its approximate coefficients are not an independently verified certificate here. The shorter-length assertion for that family is given without proof. The explicit family in Theorem 5.3 has length 4t^2+2t+1, yielding a twenty-one-qubit benchmark at t=2.
entries.checking_status: Published construction reported by the source; not re-executed in this campaign.

entries.locator: Section 2.2; Section 3.1, Conjecture 3.1 and Figures 1-2; equation (12).
entries.note: The numerical study conjectures minimum length 3t^2+3t+1. Its searches first find two-error-correcting candidates at n=19. Optimization failure at shorter lengths is not an exclusion certificate. Equation (12) recalls the quantum Singleton constraint n >= 4t+1 for a nontrivial logical code, hence n >= 9 at t=2.
entries.checking_status: The minimum-length formula is conjectural numerical evidence; the Singleton bound is a separate established bound whose applicability must be checked.

entries.locator: Proposition B2; Appendix B-B; Appendix B-D and Remark B1.
entries.note: Proposition B2 identifies codes in symmetric powers with intrinsic codes while preserving dimension and distance. Appendix B presents linear-programming constraints on intrinsic enumerators. Its distance-three example excludes lengths below seven. This is not a distance-five exclusion for all lengths below nineteen.
entries.checking_status: Published preprint framework and stated distance-three example; no distance-five certificate has been computed for this campaign.

entries.locator: Corollary 1, equation (79) in the inspected v1 HTML rendering.
entries.note: The intrinsic MacWilliams matrix is given by a terminating hypergeometric expression. In the qubit specialization, its entries can support exact linear-programming calculations at fixed n. Computing a transform alone does not prove that the relevant distance-five feasible region is empty.
entries.checking_status: Potential tool for a lower-bound approach, not a supplied solution.
